item.title: Rob Wallace | Bitcoin News – “Bitcoin Is Now In FULL Bull Mode.” | Matt Hougan
item.description:
Matt Hougan says wealth managers are about to become the next major wave of Bitcoin buyers, and he is calling it full bull mode. He also thinks there could be a twelve billion dollar single-day ETF inflow coming. But he is also warning of real chop ahead before that next leg fully takes hold.

The CIO of Bitwise returns to break down the Liquid hack and why institutional demand for Bitcoin barely blinked, why custody and white-hat ethics are becoming a serious conversation at the highest levels, and why Bessent's Treasury plan really only leads to two outcomes, both of which are bullish for Bitcoin.

Full bull mode does not mean a straight line up. This is one of the most data-driven and institutionally grounded conversations on where Bitcoin stands right now, chop and all.

Here is what we cover:

• Why wealth managers are about to become the next wave of major Bitcoin buyers

• The Liquid hack and why institutional Bitcoin demand survived it intact

• Custody, hacker negotiations, and the ethics of white-hat intervention

• How AI-powered attacks are forcing Bitcoin security to harden faster

• Why diversifying Bitcoin custody across ETFs is becoming a real strategy

• In-kind ETF transfers explained and who is using them right now

• Whether ETFs could someday transfer Bitcoin out and what that means for custody

• Is the Bitcoin bottom in, and why Matt still expects chop before the next leg up

• Bitcoin's new base and what near-term price action tells institutional investors

• ETF inflows and the next wealth manager buying cycle

• Hedge fund flows versus long-only ETF flows and why it matters

• Retail capitulation and what quarterly reporting reveals about investors

• Why the debasement trade is back and how Bitwise built an ETF around it

• Gold and Bitcoin miners as leveraged bets and rising institutional mining interest

• Why owning both AI stocks and Bitcoin makes sense right now

• Whether AI is in a late 1990s style bubble and what that means for scarce assets

• Fed versus Treasury and why the real power dynamic matters more than headlines

• Is this actually soft yield curve control in disguise

• How Bitwise gets to a $1.3 million Bitcoin price target

• What sophisticated institutions actually believe about Bitcoin right now

• Why Bitcoin is quietly becoming normal inside institutional portfolios

🔔 Subscribe for weekly Bitcoin and macro analysis.

item.title: Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock'n'Roll – Commercial Bank Money Tokens: The Missing Piece of the Tokenized Economy?
item.description:
Corporate balance sheets still run on commercial bank money, while the assets and business processes surrounding them are increasingly moving onto DLT networks. Commercial Bank Money Tokens (CBMTs) are designed to close that gap: they place a regulated bank liability directly on-chain without asking companies to adopt a fundamentally different form of money.

In this episode, Dr. Jonas Groß and Manuel Klein speak with Manfred Richels, Head of Corporate Payments at the German Savings Banks Association (DSGV), and Tim Bailey, Chief Commercial Officer at Red Date Technology and a leader of the Universal Digital Payments Network (UDPN). They explain what makes a CBMT different from a stablecoin. A CBMT remains a claim against a regulated bank, can be redeemed at par into central bank money and may be interest-bearing. The DLT record becomes the primary source of truth.

The conversation follows the token across a multi-bank transaction. When money moves from Bank A to Bank B, the first bank’s token is burned and the recipient bank issues a new token representing its own liability. Settlement between the banks follows separately in central bank money. This architecture is intended to make commercial bank money usable in smart contracts while retaining established compliance, accounting and risk-management treatment.

Richels and Bailey also discuss the live Siemens–Evonik pay-per-use pilot, where sensor data and chemical consumption trigger an automated payment; programmable delivery-versus-payment; and agentic B2B payments in which an AI agent is cryptographically linked to an accountable person or entity. They examine the expansion of the CBMT initiative beyond Germany, the role of Pontes, Appia and Project Agorá, and the likely coexistence of tokenized deposits, stablecoins, CBDCs and conventional payment rails. At stake is a practical question: can banks make deposits programmable without sacrificing the legal certainty and controls that make them useful?

item.title: The Bitcoin Matrix – Aaron Siri: The One Product You Can't Sue in America
item.description:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

item.title: The Bitcoin Standard Podcast – 342. Hardware Wallets: Security or Liability
item.description:
Saifedean hosts a debate between JW Weatherman and Giacomo Zucco on whether hardware wallets are a security liability. They discuss the Cold Card entropy backdoor, multi-vendor multisig, the code review process in Bitcoin Core, using generic laptops, and how to think about your threat model.

item.title: The Bitcoin Frontier – Inside Wall Street’s bitcoin playbook with Denny Galindo
item.description:
Denny is a wealth manager and bitcoin research lead at Morgan Stanley, where he bridges traditional finance and bitcoin for high-net-worth investors. He operates inside one of the world’s largest financial institutions while developing frameworks to help advisors understand and allocate to bitcoin.

In this episode, Denny joins The Bitcoin Frontier to share how investors should think about bitcoin in a portfolio, the three core investor buckets driving adoption, and his thoughts on determining whether you’re underweight or overweight bitcoin. We dig into bitcoin’s market cycles and seasonal framework, the role of global money supply in driving returns, and practical strategies for gaining exposure in a volatile asset.

item.title: Swan Signal Live - A Bitcoin Show – John Haar Returns: Why the Fed Must Talk Tough While It Inflates
item.description:
• John reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as a nothing burger for Bitcoiners: a Fed chair must talk tough on inflation because signaling anything else would send inflation expectations and yields higher, while the long-run path of financial repression stays the same
  • Warsh reported that 54% of PCE basket components rose more than 3% over the past year, called 4.1% unemployment full employment, and framed inflation as squarely the Fed's problem to solve
  • Markets read the speech as hawkish anyway: the two-year yield rose about 12 basis points while gold and Bitcoin each gave back roughly 3.5%
  • On last week's expanded Treasury buybacks, John points to two signals: a 30-year yield near 5.3% is clearly bothering policymakers, and the Fed has never meaningfully reduced its holdings of 10-year-plus Treasuries even during quantitative tightening, evidence that natural buyers of long-dated government paper are scarce
  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

item.title: Bitcoin Audible.DE - Die besten Bitcoin-Artikel, vorgelesen in deutscher Sprache! – 208. Martin Connor - Bitcoin, das ultimative Kollateral
item.description:
von Martin Connor – Originaltitel: «Bitcoin: The Ultimate Collateral«

*„Die beste, einfachste – ultimative – Form der Kreditsicherheit ist etwas, das sofort beansprucht und verkauft werden kann, wenn der Schuldner seine Zahlungen nicht leistet. Der Verkauf eines Hauses kann Monate oder sogar Jahre dauern. Auch Aktien haben zeitliche Beschränkungen. Bitcoin jedoch nicht. Bitcoin ist immer in Bewegung“
*

(Martin Connor)

Wenn man Bitcoin als hartes, in seinem Kern nicht veränderbares oder manipulierbares Asset begreift, welche Möglichkeiten eröffnen sich dadurch? Das Buch „Bitcoin: Die ultimative Kreditsicherheit“ untersucht, wie die Bereiche Bitcoin und Kreditvergabe perfekt zusammenpassen. Etwa, wie Bitcoin-Besitzer und Bitcoin-Unternehmen den maximalen Wert aus ihren Bitcoins herausholen können, ohne sie verkaufen zu müssen.

Wir lesen ein Kapitel aus diesem Buch, das eine zentrale Idee beleuchtet: Bitcoin als die beste Sicherheit, die die Menschheit je hatte. Die meisten Menschen denken beim Thema «Sicherheit» an Häuser, Aktien, Gold und Bargeld – aber weil es scheinbar nichts Besseres gab, übersehen sie deren enorme Schwächen. Die Kombination der Elemente von Multisignatur – echtes gemeinsames Eigentum, perfekte digitale Knappheit, Portabilität und die unübertroffene Verfügbarkeit von Bitcoin – unterscheidet es grundlegend von herkömmlichen Besicherungsmodellen.

Verkaufe Deine Bitcoins niemals – lebe davon.

Weitere Empfehlungen:

  • Pierre Rochard: «Der Nutzen des Sparens» (Ep. #019)
  • Tomer Strolight: «Warum Bitcoin?» (Ep. #80-82)
  • Saifedean Ammous: «Für eine Rückkehr zu niedriger Zeitpräferenz» (Ep. #77)
  • Pierre Rochard: «Bitcoin vs. Gold» (Ep. #71)
  • Hans-Hermann Hoppe: «Der Ertrag aus gespartem Geld – neu überdacht» (Ep. #18)
  • Parker Lewis: «Die «Bezahl‘ mich in Bitcoin!»-Theorie» (#140)
  • Parker Lewis: «Bitcoin-Zahlungen: Die ‹Jemand ist der Nächste›-Logik» (#151)
  • HodlHodl.com für Belehnung von Bitcoin, ebenso wie Unchained Capital, Ledn, Firefish etc.

Abonniere BitcoinAudible.de und empfehle unsere Vorlesungen jedem, der/die sich für Bitcoin interessiert. Hilf damit auch anderen, Bitcoin von einem starken monetären, wirtschaftlichen und philosophischen Fundament aus zu erkunden.

Unterstütze bitte unser Projekt und sende uns Sats via Lightning oder nütze eine der anderen Optionen.

Tipp: Bitcoin nur mehr KYC-frei kaufen! Auf HodlHodl.com ist das recht einfach, und mit Anmeldung über den obigen Link reduziert Du darüber hinaus sogar auch die Spesen für Deine ersten Käufe dort.

item.title: The Bitcoin Layer – The Most Important Inflation Report Of The Year
item.description: <![CDATA[In this episode, Nik explains why he thinks this week's inflation data is the most important economic release of the year, with PPI and CPI landing days before the Fed's September 16 decision. He covers why treasury bills lead the Fed and have been pricing hikes since May, how Kevin Warsh ending forward guidance leaves the market guessing into every meeting, and why core CPI running at 0.2% a month makes an immediate hike unlikely while a 0.4% print would change everything. Nik also lays out why he believes the Fed will hold, what a hiking cycle would do to liquidity, and the three sources he recommends for understanding the global balance sheet.]]>

item.title: Bitcoin Magazine Podcast – Arthur Hayes: Why Bitcoin is the Fastest Horse in the Yield Curve Control Era
item.description:
When the Treasury doubled its bond buyback out of the blue, the market read it as one thing: yield curve control by another name. Arthur Hayes joins host Spencer Nichols to walk through the mechanics, short-end issuance funding long-end buybacks, and what that implies for central bank balance sheets. His conclusion is simple. If the balance sheet expands, you want the asset most responsive to money printing, and he argues that asset is Bitcoin.

item.title: Bitcoiners - Live From Bitcoin Beach – This Bitcoin Startup in El Salvador Runs With No Bank, No KYC, and No Middleman | Jon Byrne of BitTasker
item.description:
Would you sell your house, go all in on Bitcoin, and move to El Salvador without ever setting foot in the country? Jon Byrne did exactly that. I sat down with the BitTasker founder to hear how a kid from Ireland grew up around the violence of the Troubles era, then apartheid-era Johannesburg, then the Celtic Tiger collapse, and finally took one last look at the fiat world and decided sound money was worth betting everything on.

Before selling it all, Jon had to orange pill his partner Roxanne. Every morning they'd sit down for "Coffee with Jon" and talk Bitcoin for an hour or two until the penny dropped. Then one day she told him to sell the house, buy Bitcoin, and go to El Salvador. His advice for couples on the stacking journey comes down to patience, because nobody should get dragged into a low time preference life they haven't chosen for themselves.

Then we dig into BitTasker, a KYC-free tasking app built on the Nostr protocol that helps Salvadorans earn Bitcoin instead of just buying it. No middleman ever touches the funds, and earned trust travels with you, because your reputation lives on your keys instead of some company's server.

Here's the part that earned my respect: the whole idea started when Jon met a guy in Australia who went from cleaning up dog poop on Airtasker to running a construction company. Instead of rushing to build, Jon spent a full year grinding out odd jobs on that same platform, taking the worst tasks to learn the gig economy from the inside. That's when he knew the same ladder could work even better on a Bitcoin standard, where proof of work applies to people too.

If you're thinking about your own move to El Salvador, we cover the boots-on-the-ground details too, from renewing residency barefoot at the beachside immigration office in Punta Roca to the workshops BitTasker runs at the El Zonte community center right here in Bitcoin Beach. Jon's also plugging into the circular economy movement in Costa Rica, Brazil, Ireland, and beyond. If this one has you ready to sell the house and buy Bitcoin, maybe have a few coffees with your spouse first. Then subscribe, share it with a friend who's still stuck in fiat, and drop a comment: would you move to a country you'd never visited?

—Bitcoin Beach Team

item.title: Unchained – Uneasy Money: Is OpenAI Training on Your Private Chats to Win the AI Race?
item.description:
Alex Thorn and Jon join Kain and Taylor to unpack a Bitcoin hack, two new frontier models, and why nobody trusts their AI chats anymore.

========================================================

Thank you to our sponsors!


Visit 1inch to swap tokenized securities, crypto and more. Simple. Secure. Self-custodial. Whatever asset you’re buying - swap it at ⁠⁠⁠http://unchainedcrypto.com/go/1inch-sn⁠⁠⁠

========================================================

A Bitcoin sidechain lost $300 million to a consensus bug this week, and the hackers who returned 85% of it are trying to extort a "bug bounty" out of Blockstream for the rest.

Alex Thorn, Head of Firmwide Research at Galaxy, and Jon, Head of Strategy at Venice and co-founder of ShapeShift, join Kain Warwick and Taylor Monahan to unpack how AI models are now finding exploits faster than the humans who wrote the code, and to push back on the idea that returning stolen funds makes anyone a white hat.

They also dig into Astra and Fable 5.1, two frontier models that landed days after a mathematician working inside OpenAI's Codex clashed publicly with OpenAI over who actually solved a Millennium Prize-adjacent proof. 

Jon and Alex explain why the "don't train on my data" toggle may not mean much, and why identity is becoming the real privacy battleground.

The conversation closes on whether an Anthropic researcher quitting this week is a warning the industry is choosing to ignore.

Thank you to our sponsors!


Visit 1inch to swap tokenized securities, crypto and more. Simple. Secure. Self-custodial. Whatever asset you’re buying - swap it at ⁠⁠⁠http://unchainedcrypto.com/go/1inch-sn⁠⁠⁠

========================================================

A Bitcoin sidechain lost $300 million to a consensus bug this week, and the hackers who returned 85% of it are trying to extort a "bug bounty" out of Blockstream for the rest.

Alex Thorn, Head of Firmwide Research at Galaxy, and Jon, Head of Strategy at Venice and co-founder of ShapeShift, join Kain Warwick and Taylor Monahan to unpack how AI models are now finding exploits faster than the humans who wrote the code, and to push back on the idea that returning stolen funds makes anyone a white hat.

They also dig into Astra and Fable 5.1, two frontier models that landed days after a mathematician working inside OpenAI's Codex clashed publicly with OpenAI over who actually solved a Millennium Prize-adjacent proof. 

Jon and Alex explain why the "don't train on my data" toggle may not mean much, and why identity is becoming the real privacy battleground.

The conversation closes on whether an Anthropic researcher quitting this week is a warning the industry is choosing to ignore.

item.title: The "What is Money?" Show – The 3 Hidden Languages That Control Reality w/ Neal Flesher
item.description:
Robert Breedlove drops listeners into a raw call with Neil Flesher, his co-author on the upcoming book "The Right Way to Make Money". Their project explores human nature and reality through three languages: literacy, numeracy, and money.

Using music as their central metaphor, they discuss how harmony reveals what mathematics alone cannot, why virtue requires both difference and relation, and what happens when a society loses its common measure. The conversation weaves together philosophy, Austrian economics, and natural law—ultimately framing Bitcoin as civilization's "common tuning fork."

item.title: The Bitcoin Way Podcast – Hacker Steals $320M of Blockstream's BTC | Bitcoin Banter
item.description:
A self-proclaimed white hat hacker exploited Blockstream's Liquid Network, minting fake LBTC and draining nearly 4,000 Bitcoin worth around $320M. The funds were held on-chain during public negotiations conducted through blockchain messages, with 85% eventually returned and around 600 BTC kept as a claimed 'consultancy fee'.

This breakdown explains how the Liquid hack happened, what it reveals about federated sidechains, custodial risk, and Bitcoin security. We also cover UK mandatory phone surveillance and digital ID proposals, arrests for communications offenses, rising Europe-Russia tensions, LG TV privacy concerns, plus our Donkeys of the Week, who are offering the opportunity to own a brand new meme coin and pair of Strategy-branded shoes.

item.title: House of Satoshi - Bitcoin und Friends – BTCAI SPECIAL #1 - Warum BTCAI?
item.description:
Marketingmaterial

Bitcoin, wenn es läuft. Cash, wenn es kracht. Die Idee dazu ist nicht am Reissbrett entstanden, sondern in einem Seminarraum.

In der ersten Episode zu BTCAI ist unser Host & Gründer Rino Borini, zu Gast. Durch den Podcast führt Luca Brun, Channel and Ecosystem Manager im House of Satoshi.


Darum geht es:

  • Wie die Idee aus über 2500 ausgebildeten Teilnehmern entstanden ist
  • Warum Bitcoin only, obwohl die Rückrechnung mit Ethereum besser war
  • Für wen das Produkt gebaut ist, inklusive der Maxis
  • Warum aisot die Strategie liefert und nicht das House of Satoshi selbst
  • Selbstverwahrung gegen ETP: Widerspruch oder nicht
  • Zeichnung, Startpreis und Börsengang Schritt für Schritt


Und die Ansage: Kosten offenlegen, keine Garantien versprechen, auch dann hinstehen, wenn die Maschine einen Monat zu spät reagiert.


Alle Infos zu BTCAI: http://www.btcai-etp.ch

Mehr zu House of Satoshi: http://www.house-of-satoshi.ch


Folge dem Podcast und hinterlasse eine Bewertung, das hilft uns enorm. 🙏


𝘞𝘦𝘳𝘣𝘶𝘯𝘨 𝘨𝘦𝘮ä𝘴𝘴 𝘈𝘳𝘵. 68 𝘍𝘐𝘋𝘓𝘌𝘎. 𝘈𝘶𝘴𝘴𝘤𝘩𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘭𝘪𝘤𝘩 𝘧ü𝘳 𝘗𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘯 𝘮𝘪𝘵 𝘞𝘰𝘩𝘯𝘴𝘪𝘵𝘻 𝘚𝘤𝘩𝘸𝘦𝘪𝘻, 𝘯𝘪𝘤𝘩𝘵 𝘧ü𝘳 𝘜𝘚-𝘗𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘯 𝘣𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘮𝘮𝘵. 𝘉𝘛𝘊𝘈𝘐 𝘪𝘴𝘵 𝘬𝘦𝘪𝘯 𝘗𝘳𝘰𝘥𝘶𝘬𝘵 𝘯𝘢𝘤𝘩 𝘒𝘰𝘭𝘭𝘦𝘬𝘵𝘪𝘷𝘢𝘯𝘭𝘢𝘨𝘦𝘯𝘨𝘦𝘴𝘦𝘵𝘻 (𝘒𝘈𝘎) 𝘶𝘯𝘥 𝘶𝘯𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘩𝘵 𝘯𝘪𝘤𝘩𝘵 𝘥𝘦𝘳 𝘈𝘶𝘧𝘴𝘪𝘤𝘩𝘵 𝘥𝘦𝘳 𝘍𝘐𝘕𝘔𝘈, 𝘦𝘪𝘯𝘻𝘪𝘨 𝘥𝘪𝘦 𝘝𝘦𝘳𝘸𝘢𝘩𝘳𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘯 𝘚𝘸𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘲𝘶𝘰𝘵𝘦 𝘪𝘴𝘵 𝘍𝘐𝘕𝘔𝘈-𝘣𝘦𝘢𝘶𝘧𝘴𝘪𝘤𝘩𝘵𝘪𝘨𝘵. 𝘉𝘪𝘵𝘤𝘰𝘪𝘯 𝘣𝘭𝘦𝘪𝘣𝘵 𝘷𝘰𝘭𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘭, 𝘦𝘪𝘯 𝘒𝘢𝘱𝘪𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘷𝘦𝘳𝘭𝘶𝘴𝘵 𝘪𝘴𝘵 𝘮ö𝘨𝘭𝘪𝘤𝘩. 𝘔𝘢𝘴𝘴𝘨𝘦𝘣𝘭𝘪𝘤𝘩 𝘪𝘴𝘵 𝘥𝘢𝘴 𝘛𝘦𝘳𝘮𝘴𝘩𝘦𝘦𝘵 (Final Terms).


]]>

item.title: bitcoin ist - Wissen statt FOMO – 22) ... eine Frage der Sicherheit
item.description:
Wo liegt eigentlich das größte Sicherheitsrisiko bei Bitcoin?

Das Netzwerk ist sicher, das haben wir in Folge 21 geklärt. Aber wie sicher ist eigentlich die Art, wie du deine eigenen Bitcoin verwahrst? Anlass für diese Folge ist ein aktueller Vorfall: Bei einer bekannten Hardware-Wallet wurden durch einen jahrelang unentdeckten Fehler in der Firmware Bitcoin im Millionenwert entwendet, ganz ohne physischen Zugriff auf die Geräte. Wir sprechen darüber, was das für die Themen Open Source, Vertrauen und Eigenverwahrung bedeutet.

Themen in dieser Folge:

  • "Not your keys, not your coins" - warum Eigenverwahrung wichtig ist.
  • Der aktuelle Sicherheitsvorfall bei einer Hardware-Wallet (Stand: August 2026)
  • Der Unterschied zwischen "einsehbarem" und wirklich freiem Open-Source-Code
  • Warum Vertrauen bei Bitcoin-Produkten nie ganz wegfällt, auch bei guter Sicherheit
  • Die Balance zwischen Sicherheit und Praktikabilität beim eigenen Wallet-Setup


Alles von "bitcoin ist..." ⁠⁠Hier geht es zu allen meinen Kanälen⁠⁠

Einsteiger-Spezial: möchtest du wissen, WIE man bitcoin sicher kauft und verwahrt? ⁠⁠Kostenlose und sichere Kaufanleitung direkt in dein Postfach ⁠⁠

Hinterlasse mir gerne eine 5-Sterne-Bewertung oder einen Kommentar.

Danke, Dein Christian.

]]>

item.title: Der Bitcoin Kompass: Wegweiser im Kaninchenbau – Folge 5: Der Bitcoin-Preis – Zwischen Angebot, Nachfrage und Geldpolitik
item.description:
Was bestimmt eigentlich den Bitcoin-Preis? In Folge 5 vom Bitcoin-Kompass sprechen wir üeber eines der meistdiskutierten Themen im Bitcoin-Space: den Preis. Dabei geht es nicht um Prognosen oder Kaufempfehlungen, sondern um ein grundlegendes Verständnis dafüer, wie der Bitcoin-Preis entsteht und welche Kraefte ihn beeinflussen.


Wir erklären, wie Angebot und Nachfrage auf Bitcoin-Börsen funktionieren, warum das Handelsvolumen oft wichtiger ist als der Preis selbst und welche Rolle die Marktkapitalisierung spielt. Ausserdem beleuchten wir die grossen Einflussfaktoren: das Bitcoin-Halving und den Vier-Jahres-Zyklus, die Geldpolitik der US-Notenbank (Fed), Inflation und die wachsenden Staatsschulden der USA. Im Vergleich zwischen Bitcoin und Gold zeigen sie, warum Bitcoin technologisch ueberlegen sein könnte - und warum der Preis letztlich ein Spiegel des wachsenden Vertrauens in diese neue Technologie ist.


Mehr Infos, interaktive Grafiken zur Marktkapitalisierung und Kontaktmoeglichkeiten findet ihr auf:


Webseite: https://derbitcoinkompass.ch

E-Mail: kontakt@derbitcoinkompass.ch

Telegram: https://t.me/btc_kaninchenbau


Feedback und Fragen gerne per E-Mail, ueber Telegram oder ueber unsere Webseite.



(00:00:00) Begruessung & Einfuehrung ins Thema Preis

(00:01:31) Volatilitaet und der aktuelle Bitcoin-Preis

(00:02:33) Kaufkraft, Inflation und warum Menschen investieren

(00:05:20) Marktkapitalisierung: Bitcoin vs. Gold vs. Immobilien vs. Aktien

(00:08:05) Wie entsteht der Bitcoin-Preis? Angebot & Nachfrage erklaert

(00:11:04) Warum das Handelsvolumen entscheidend ist

(00:12:43) Die grossen Einflussfaktoren auf den Bitcoin-Preis

(00:13:26) In was messen wir den Preis? Euro, Dollar oder Aepfel?

(00:17:03) Warum Geld kein stabiler Massstab ist

(00:18:10) Bitcoins festes Angebot: Maximal 21 Millionen

(00:20:02) Das Halving und der Vier-Jahres-Zyklus

(00:24:22) Die Fed, Zinspolitik und US-Staatsschulden

(00:31:27) Was bedeutet das alles fuer den Bitcoin-Preis?

(00:33:37) Bitcoin vs. Gold: Vorteile und Unterschiede

(00:40:30) Preisprognose: Bitcoin auf 1 Million Dollar?

(00:41:54) Zusammenfassung & Verabschiedung

item.title: The Bitcoin Infinity Show – Bitcoin Won't Be Money Until 2080 | Cory Klippsten | BIS #219
item.description:
Cory Klippsten joins the Bitcoin Infinity Show to talk about Swan's Fifty Days for Freedom campaign, the parallels he draws between the American founders' fight for political independence and this generation's fight for monetary independence, and why he thinks Bitcoin adoption follows a seventy to eighty year technological revolution curve rather than a sudden dollar collapse. He and Knut get into KYC, honeypots and self-custody, the recent wave of VPN bans and age verification laws, and why chain analysis firms may be selling a certainty they cannot actually deliver. They also cover the three functions of money and whether store of value and medium of exchange were ever really separate, the case for ten million Bitcoiners as an intransigent minority, and why Cory thinks the dollar's network effect is getting stronger even as Bitcoin remains the fastest horse in the race.

item.title: THE Bitcoin Podcast – BITCOIN RED TEAM: The AI Arms Race for Open-Source Security | Rob Hamilton
item.description:
The Coldcard vulnerability became the catalyst for one of the largest AI-powered security efforts in Bitcoin's history.

Walker America sits down with Rob Hamilton (AnchorWatch) to unpack Bitcoin's volunteer "Red Team," the future of Bitcoin security and self-custody, AI-powered vulnerability research, open-source software security, Kimi K3 vs. OpenAI, responsible disclosure, collaborative custody, and why the emerging AI arms race could fundamentally reshape cybersecurity far beyond Bitcoin.

  • The Coldcard vulnerability and what actually happened
  • Bitcoin's volunteer Red Team and AI-powered security audits

item.title: BITCOIN & ALTCOINS – Basis für den nächsten Aufwärtsschub steht
item.description:
Geduld bleibt am Kryptomarkt derzeit gefragt: Nach dem jüngsten Ausbruch bewegt sich der Markt weitgehend seitwärts. Doch im Hintergrund werden bereits die Weichen für die nächste Aufwärtsbewegung gestellt.

In der aktuellen Folge von „Bitcoin & Altcoins“ spricht Oliver Michel (tokentus investment AG) darüber, welche Ereignisse und Entwicklungen für eine Fortsetzung der bullishen Phase entscheidend sind, welcher Coin überraschend stark zugelegt hat und worauf sich Anleger in den kommenden Tagen einstellen sollten.

Hinweis: Die im Podcast besprochenen Coins und Token stellen keine spezifischen Kauf- oder Anlageempfehlungen dar. Die Moderatoren oder der Verlag haften nicht für etwaige Verluste, die aufgrund der Umsetzung der im Podcast diskutierten Gedanken oder Ideen entstehen.

Das Gespräch wurde am 11.08.20226 an der Frankfurter Börse aufgezeichnet.

Tägliche Informationen gefällig? Dann ab zu „Krypto-Insights“ – dem Telegram-Kanal von Oliver Michel und Johanna Krämer. Weitere Infos unter krypto-insights.de

item.title: The Café Bitcoin Podcast – The Finale: Liquid's 4,000 Bitcoin, the Caching Bug, and 50 Days for Freedom Wrapped
item.description:
• The last day. Brady opened with the count, 37 shows in 50 days, and the campaign's frame: political independence 250 years ago, monetary independence now. Yan Pritzker, Frank Corva, Suze and Alec on stage; Unseen Finance returned at the end.
  • The Liquid hack, plainly. On Sunday somebody sent 4,000 L-BTC to SideSwap's peg-out and the Liquid Federation paid out real Bitcoin. The L-BTC had been created from nothing. Blockstream paused the sidechain and 3,400 Bitcoin came back Monday.
  • ⭐ Yan on what broke: a caching bug, not anyone's keys. "The only two hard problems in computer science are naming and cache invalidation." Two transactions shared one cache key, so validators mistook a fake for one already checked.
  • Why it is not Bitcoin. Yan: Liquid is an 11-of-15 federation of companies with its own database and rules. "This is a separate thing, this is not Bitcoin itself." Lightning is built on Bitcoin script; Liquid is not.
  • ⭐ Frank on the 15%. The hackers returned 85% and kept about 600 Bitcoin. His question: will anyone be made whole, and if they keep it, "they're surely not white hats." A Bitcoin Policy Institute lawyer offered to talk.
  • Yan's verdict on the hat color: gray. Taking everything to beat a black hat is arguable. Keeping a cut is not. "You don't just return a wallet and take a bunch of stuff out of it."
  • Suze's question: Bitcoiners are ruthless about added trust assumptions, so why did Liquid get a pass? "Were we discerning enough?" Leave the base layer and you take on another code base and another set of failure points.
  • ⭐ Yan on open source in the AI era: it stays because every open project gets red-teamed by the whole internet. Closed systems get hacked too, "we just don't hear about them." The base chain is "the ultimate boss" nobody has beaten.
  • Yan's bank numbers, read live from the Identity Theft Resource Center: 3,332 reported data compromises in 2025 affecting 280 million people, 739 of them in financial services. "Bank-grade security" is not a standard anyone actually meets.
  • ⭐ Frank's hard question: must the layers be as bulletproof as Bitcoin? Yan: nothing is, and the only path is slow growth. Bitcoin was attacked at $1, then $10,000, then a billion. Early adopters carry the risk.
  • Yan's rocket-ship rule. Bitcoin Core engineering is closer to launching a spacecraft than shipping web software. "Years of careful review, study, simulations on other chains." Test new tech on other coins for two years first.
  • Suze asked whether ossification risks losing the skills to change Bitcoin in 50 years. Frank and Yan: no. Ossification is no new features, not no developers, and AI has widened who can work on cryptography and game theory.
  • Yan on open-weight versus hosted AI: the same debate as open source versus closed, and open source won the internet. His advice to companies: externalize memory, skills and harness so you can swap models. Swan built its own.
  • Unseen Finance returned with a proposal: these incidents are a credibility problem for the services on top of Bitcoin, not for Bitcoin. His fix, borrowed from banking: a self-regulatory body plus an insurance pool that service providers pay into.
  • Brady's tally at the close: Cory, Yan, Steve, Alec, Isaiah, Matt and Brandon from Swan; Larry Lepard three times; Parker Lewis, Daniel Batten, Tom and Callum, Guy Swann, Ryan MacLeod, Alana, Bob Burnett, Roxana. Suze made 35 of 37.
  • The close. "We have the tools, we have the knowledge, we have the culture, we have the determination." The half-price buy fee ends today; limit orders placed today keep it. Yan's last word: take security seriously, "go play with AI."
    • ]]>

item.title: Surfin' Bitcoin – La bulle de l'IA va éclater
item.description:
Nicolas Bouzou, économiste et directeur du cabinet Astérès, pose un diagnostic sans filtre sur l'état des finances publiques françaises et sur ce qu'il faut faire de son argent en 2026.


Dette hors de contrôle, taxation des riches, réforme des retraites, tsunami de l'IA, bulle des valorisations tech, Bitcoin. Il répond sans langue de bois, et il n'est pas toujours d'accord avec moi.


⚠️ Cette vidéo n'est pas un conseil en investissement.


📌 DANS CET ÉPISODE, VOUS APPRENDREZ :


➤ Pourquoi nos finances publiques ne sont plus seulement dégradées, mais « hors de contrôle ».

➤ Ce qu'il ferait s'il était président en 2027, en s'inspirant de la méthode de Gaulle-Pinay de 1958.

➤ Pourquoi taxer les riches est selon lui une impasse technique.

➤ Emmanuel Macron a-t-il menti aux entrepreneurs ?

➤ Comment l'effet Cantillon décide de qui s'enrichit et de qui s'appauvrit quand on crée de la monnaie.

➤ Pourquoi le vrai problème du pouvoir d'achat français est un problème de productivité, pas de marges d'entreprise.

➤ Son pronostic sur l'IA, et pourquoi il refuse de parler de « job apocalypse ».

➤ Pourquoi il pense qu'il y a une bulle de l'IA, qu'elle va éclater, et que c'est une bonne nouvelle.

➤ Ce qu'il pense vraiment du Bitcoin, et pourquoi il n'en détient pas encore.

➤ Comment il répartit réellement son patrimoine.


👉 Formation « Investir en Bitcoin » → https://www.investir-en-bitcoin.com/ibtc-replay5


⏱️ CHAPITRES


00:00 Introduction et présentation de Nicolas Bouzou


PARTIE 1 · LA DETTE ET L'ÉTAT

02:50 Son diagnostic sur les finances publiques

05:55 Ce qu'il ferait s'il était président en 2027

08:34 Faut-il taxer les riches ?

12:25 La France est-elle vraiment injuste fiscalement ?

15:00 Le désaccord sur Macron


PARTIE 2 · POUVOIR D'ACHAT ET IA

18:05 D'où vient vraiment la perte de pouvoir d'achat

21:28 Salaires, productivité et coût de l'État providence

24:59 L'impact de l'IA dans les entreprises

28:32 La « job apocalypse » aura-t-elle lieu ?

32:12 Ce que l'IA pourrait changer dans l'État


PARTIE 3 · OÙ PLACER SON ARGENT

35:32 Et si tout ça était une bulle ?

40:15 Ce qu'il pense vraiment du Bitcoin

44:09 Sa méthode d'investissement

46:46 La répartition de son patrimoine

item.title: The Peter McCormack Show – #211 - Jim Al-Khalili - Reality Is An Illusion: Quantum Entanglement, Time & Dark Energy
item.description:
Prof. Jim Al-Khalili is a theoretical physicist, author, and public broadcaster who holds a chair in physics at the University of Surrey. Known for his BBC documentaries and popular science books, including On Time and The World According to Physics, his work spans quantum mechanics, nuclear reaction theory, and the fundamental nature of space-time.  


Jim and I discuss the divide between psychological "manifest time" and the laws of physics. Jim explains general relativity, gravitational time dilation, and the astrophysics behind Interstellar, before tackling the mathematical conflict between general relativity and quantum mechanics. Jim breaks down quantum entanglement, Bell’s Inequality, and competing models of reality-from the Copenhagen view to the Many-Worlds interpretation. Finally, we discuss how AI systems are formalizing complex mathematical theorems and processing deep-space data to decode dark matter and dark energy.


- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

item.title: Bitcoin Fortress – BF232 - Bitcoin is Becoming the Escape Valve - 9/6/26
item.description:
Date: September 6, 2026
Block Height: 965807
Moscow Time: 1254
Fees: 1 / 1 /2

 

In this episode, we look at a week where Bitcoin increasingly behaved like an escape valve from a strained monetary system. We cover the strong jobs report and renewed Fed pressure, rising Bitcoin-gold correlation, institutional adoption, corporate treasury accumulation, the CLARITY Act, El Salvador, the Trezor privacy breach, and the growing role of Bitcoin in places where traditional banking simply doesn’t work. Plus, we check in on the Bitcoin podcast universe, feature this week’s Bitcoin Fortress Substack, and talk about the new book, The Sovereign Life.

 

Bitcoin Fortress YouTube Channel:

https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCEPGN1YCIQcMxkUig5GaNrQ

 

Bitcoin Fortress Substack Featured Post:

The Family as a Sovereign Institution
https://bitcoinfortress.substack.com/p/the-family-as-a-sovereign-institution

 

Bitcoin Fortress Books:

  • Bitcoin Fortress: A Simple Guide to Bitcoin for Beginners
  • Bitcoin Retirement and Estate Planning

item.title: Krypto Corner – Bitcoin, ETF und NFT: Sicher investieren - Krypto verstehen und sicher starten – Episode #13: Zeichnen mit Gewichten – Warum Rebalancing dich vor dem nächsten Krypto-Crash rettet
item.description:
Wir zeigen dir die meisterhafte Disziplin des "Rebalancings". Anstatt dich von der nackten Gier treiben zu lassen, lernst du heute, stur und roboterhaft deine ursprüngliche Risikoverteilung wiederherzustellen. Wir vergleichen zeitbasierte und schwellenbasierte (Threshold) Methoden und erklären die brutale Psychologie dahinter: Warum es so extrem schmerzhaft ist, die absoluten Gewinner zu verkaufen und ausgerechnet die Verlierer nachzukaufen – und warum genau dieser antizyklische Schmerz der einzige Weg zum langfristigen, sicheren Reichtum ist.

Doch höchste Vorsicht vor dem Finanzamt! Im großen Steuer-Deep-Dive dieser Folge warnen wir eindringlich davor, in Deutschland blind und euphorisch umzuschichten. Wir erklären im Detail, warum der direkte Tausch von Meme-Coins in harten Bitcoin sofort die 1-Jahres-Frist zerstört und die volle Steuerpflicht auslöst, und wie du dich mit "Cashflow Rebalancing" durch frisches Geld vor dem Ruin schützen kannst. Zudem beleuchten wir den paradiesischen Vorteil für Anleger in Österreich, für die Krypto-zu-Krypto-Swaps innerhalb der Börse völlig steuerneutral bleiben.

In dieser Folge erfährst du: • Warum dein Krypto-Portfolio von ganz alleine "auseinanderdriftet" und dich heimlich in ein enormes, lebensbedrohliches Risiko stürzt. • Die Profi-Methoden des zeitbasierten und schwellenbasierten (Threshold) Rebalancings. • Die Psychologie des antizyklischen Handelns: "Buy low, sell high" in der harten, schmerzhaften Praxis. • Wie das Finanzamt in DE Rebalancing als sofortigen Verkauf wertet und die fiese FiFo-Falle zuschnappen lässt. • Warum österreichische Anleger beim ständigen Umschichten einen gigantischen, steuerneutralen Marktvorteil genießen.

Diese Episode basiert auf Kapitel 13 des Einsteiger-Romans „Krypto verstehen – sicher starten. Band 1“ von Sascha Swen Heiter. Verantwortung steht über Spekulation. Haltet die Balance im Portfolio, sichert eure enormen Gewinne rechtzeitig bevor der Markt dreht, und investiert immer mit Köpfchen!

📚 Das Buch zur Show: Wenn du das gesamte Wissen sofort anwenden möchtest – von der Einrichtung deiner Hardware Wallets über die Nutzung von Burner Wallets bis hin zu wichtigen rechtlichen und steuerlichen Themen in der DACH-Region – hol dir das komplette Buch! 👉 https://amzn.eu/d/06DuLLUw

🔗 FOLGE MIR FÜR MEHR KRYPTO-WISSEN: • Spotify:https://open.spotify.com/show/5MOMwCZpWNvm6J52jkdLcl?si=yq7YoMyZSnWCg_xrVLcnww • Apple Podcasts:https://podcasts.apple.com/de/podcast/krypto-corner-bitcoin-etf-und-nft-sicher-investieren/id1872914214 • Instagram:https://instagram.com/Swen_Heiter

item.title: Epicenter - Learn about Crypto, Blockchain, Ethereum, Bitcoin and Distributed Technologies – The DAO Security Fund: Turning a Historic Hack into Ethereum's Future | Griff Green
item.description:
Ten years after The DAO hack changed Ethereum forever, Griff Green returns to Epicenter to discuss the next chapter: the DAO Security Fund.


As a co-initiator of The DAO, Griff shares the untold story of recovering funds after the hack, why over 75,000 ETH remained untouched for years, and how its staking yield is now funding public goods for Ethereum security. The conversation also explores a provocative idea: Ethereum is incredibly secure—but still not safe for everyday users.


Topics covered:

1. The inside story of The DAO and its recovery

2. Why the DAO hack may be the only hack where everyone made money

3. The DAO Security Fund and funding Ethereum security

4. Quadratic funding, grants & public goods

5. Why phishing and UX remain Ethereum's biggest weakness

6. Can Ethereum become safer than traditional banks?

7. The future of safer wallets, OpSec, and the Ethereum Economic Zone


If you enjoyed the episode, don't forget to subscribe for more conversations with the builders, founders and investors shaping the future of crypto.

item.title: The Bitcoin Boomers – What Actually Backs Bitcoin?
item.description:
"Not today you don't." The Boomers open with the question every holder secretly googles — do you owe taxes on Bitcoin you never sold? — and the answer detours through gold teeth, seventeen nuclear aircraft carriers, and Larry calmly explaining why he thinks this asset goes to a million dollars… then ten. Bob puts a number on the network nobody can picture (900 exahashes — more raw computation than every supercomputer on Earth combined), George explains why that's "the magic of Bitcoin," and then the fork question lands: what actually happened at block 961,632 when BIP-110 tried to split the chain — and why one side kept mining forever while the other managed two blocks.

Lightning-round episode: taxes, hashrate, gold vs Bitcoin, the 50% drawdown rule, estate planning without losing your keys, and one bonus question that gets a very honest answer. Larry Lepard, Bob Burnett, and George Bodine hold the couch — Gary Leland sits this one out (he'll be back).

CHAPTERS

00:00 — Cold Open

00:50 — Do I Pay Taxes on Bitcoin If I Don't Sell?

02:21 — Swan (sponsor)

03:01 — Gold vs Bitcoin: Which Do You Trust?

04:29 — 900 Exahashes & 17 Aircraft Carriers

06:51 — Sazmining (sponsor)

07:25 — What Backs Bitcoin?

10:12 — Sleeping Through 50% Drawdowns

14:33 — Ledn (sponsor)

15:01 — Bonus: The BIP-110 Fork at Block 961,632

The Bitcoin Boomers is a panel for smart, successful people over 40 still on the outside of Bitcoin looking in. Plain English answers to the questions no one else will touch. Signal without the noise.

Your hosts:

Gary Leland, founder of BitBlockBoom and Hall of Fame podcaster.

Lawrence Lepard, sound money fund manager and author of The Big Print.

Bob Burnett, mining entrepreneur and founder of Barefoot Mining.

George Bodine, the World's Most Interesting Bitcoiner.

Listen to the audio anywhere:

🍎 Apple: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-bitcoin-boomers/id1853058330

⚡ Fountain: https://fountain.fm/show/kHBRZl0Mb0MGWMELtjw4

Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@BTCBoomers

Sponsors who make Boomers possible:

Sazmining, mine your own Bitcoin: https://Sazmining.com/Boomers

Ledn, borrow against your Bitcoin: https://ledn.io/boomers

Swan, Invest in Bitcoin: https://www.swan.com/boomers

Follow the hosts:

Bob Burnett https://x.com/boomer_btc | Gary Leland https://x.com/GaryLeland | Lawrence Lepard https://x.com/LawrenceLepard | George Bodine https://x.com/Jethroe111

Educational only. Not financial, legal, tax, or investment advice. Do your own research.

item.title: POD256 | Bitcoin Mining, Freedom Tech, and Awesome Tangents – 124. Mining Forks, Firmware Red Teams, and the Future of Sovereign Hashrate
item.description:
In this episode, we dug into the latest fallout around Ocean Mining and Luke Dashjr’s departure as CTO, along with the broader controversy around BIP 110 and the so-called “LukeCoin” proof-of-work fork. We talked through why the messaging around that fork is so misleading, how term redefinition keeps confusing newer Bitcoiners, and why simply changing mining algorithms does not magically solve centralization. We also explored the technical choices behind the proposed proof-of-work change, why existing ASIC availability matters, and how these alt-fork experiments often reveal more about incentives and market structure than about any real path forward for Bitcoin.

We also spent time on the 256 Foundation’s latest work, including red-team analysis of closed-source mining firmware and why these opaque systems create serious operational and even grid-level risks. From there, we highlighted the upside of open-source firmware through Riot’s new solar-responsive mining product built on Mujina, which shows what becomes possible when miners can actually control their hardware. We wrapped with updates on the Buzz relay for agent-assisted collaboration, thoughts on making it easier for home miners to run their own low-cost nodes, and some early findings from reverse engineering a WhatsMiner M64 that suggest just how far manufacturers are going to lock users out of their own machines.

]]>

item.title: Should I Invest in Bitcoin? Grow Your Wealth & Understand the Cryptocurrency Bit Coin, for Millennials Serious About Money and Investing – Bitcoin Made Working Feel Pointless - Now I Am Taking a Huge Pay Cut and Paying the Price (Bit Coin, Wealth & Investing)
item.description:
This is a vulnerable one. I sold my plumbing business the same year Bitcoin five or six x'd, and somewhere in that overlap I quietly decided I didn't need to work as hard as I used to. I was wrong, and it's costing me right now.

In this episode you will discover:

  • Why Bitcoin is not an income strategy no matter how much it goes up, and the exact moment I forgot that despite knowing it and saying it on this podcast for years
  • Why I stopped building an emergency fund in cash and gold because I told myself I could just sell a bit of Bitcoin if anything went wrong, and why that is one of the dumbest things a Bitcoin holder can do
  • The real cost of checking out of income for a year and a half, including a job offer I actually turned down, and why selling Bitcoin to fund a lifestyle is exactly like selling your house to spend the equity

I built a free calculator that shows exactly what consistent monthly Bitcoin investing could do to your wealth over 5, 10 or 20 years. It's called the Steady Stack Calculator — punch in what you can afford to put in each month and see what the numbers actually look like at the other end. Most people are genuinely surprised. You can also download the 10 Bitcoin Mistakes to Avoid document completely free at the same link.

Steady Stack Calculator and 10 Bitcoin Mistakes Document — click here to grab both for free

Hit follow, so you never miss the latest insights on money, finance, invest and build wealth - plus clear guidance on cryptocurrency, Bitcoin, and Bit Coin for today’s serious investors.

item.title: Thank God for Bitcoin – TGFB Episode 81: Giacomo Zucco: the Metaphysical Paleo-libertarian and Black-market Supremacist
item.description:
Giacomo Zucco, President of @planb_network, shares his journey from his Catholic upbringing in Italy and how it shaped his early views on faith, his later dalliance with nihilism during his teenage years, and his eventual return to Christianity. He discusses how authors like G.K Chesterton and C.S. Lewis played pivotal roles in his intellectual journey. The dialogue also touches on contemporary political dynamics, the pendulum swing between virtue and freedom, and the rise of new political figures in response to societal changes. Giacomo discusses the importance of balancing virtue and freedom, and reflects on just how easy it is to destroy things and so difficult to build.

item.title: 21Focus - Der Bitcoin-Unternehmer Podcast – Aus der Banken IT in die Welt von Bitcoin - Harald Betz
item.description:
Folge #61 – Ein Gespräch über Banken IT und Bitcoin Bücher

Harald Beetz ist seit fast 20 Jahren selbstständig in der Beratung für Banken und Rechenzentren. Angefangen als Banklehrling bei der Sparkasse, hat er früh den Wandel von Beratung hin zu reinem Vertrieb erlebt und sich auf IT-Projekte spezialisiert. In diesem Gespräch erzählt er, wie er von der Banken IT zu Bitcoin kam, warum er mit seiner Frau einen Roman über Geld schrieb und wie er sich heute zwischen Beratung und Content rund um Bitcoin positioniert.


Du erfährst,

  • wie Harald die Bankenwelt von innen erlebt hat,
  • welche Herausforderungen und Chancen es als IT-Berater gibt,
  • warum er Bitcoin zunächst wieder verkaufte und später mit völlig anderem Blick neu entdeckte,
  • wie aus einer Buchidee seiner Frau ein gemeinsames Projekt wurde
  • und welche unternehmerischen Lektionen er aus fast zwei Jahrzehnten Selbstständigkeit mitnimmt.

item.title: 21talk – Die große Enteignung: Warum die Mittelschicht stirbt & Bitcoin die einzige Lösung ist!
item.description: <![CDATA[In diesem 21talk tauchen Jefim Gewiet und Konstantin Schmelz tief in die Welt des institutionellen Investierens und die fundamentale Bedeutung von Bitcoin ein. Jefim berichtet von seinen Erfahrungen aus dem Bereich der Family Offices und erklärt anschaulich, warum er Bitcoin für das „ehrlichste Asset der Welt“ hält. Dabei vergleichen die beiden Bitcoin mit klassischen Wertspeichern wie Gold und Immobilien und beleuchten, warum die digitale Knappheit und Verifizierbarkeit des Netzwerks eine neue Ära für das globale Finanzsystem einläuten.Darüber hinaus diskutieren sie die praktischen Anwendungen von Bitcoin im Treasury Management für Unternehmen und wie eine niedrige Zeitpräferenz das Konsumverhalten sowie die Gesellschaft langfristig positiv verändern kann. Von geopolitischen Aspekten bis hin zur individuellen finanziellen Freiheit. Dieses Gespräch bietet eine umfassende Analyse, warum Bitcoin weit mehr als nur ein Spekulationsobjekt ist. Es ist ein Plädoyer für ein faireres, technologisches Geldsystem, das ohne zentrale Instanzen funktioniert.(00:00) Intro(01:09) Milliarden-Transfer: Wie deutsches Steuergeld nach China floss(02:40) Der erste Kontakt zu Bitcoin(03:56) Family Office Insights(04:51) Warum Institutionen 2015 noch skeptisch waren(07:42) Warum Angriffe das Bitcoin-Netzwerk nur stärker machen(10:02) Milliarden-Verwaltung(12:11) Wie Bitcoin Immobilien-Finanzierungen revolutioniert(14:07) Globales Wettrennen(16:16) Bitcoin vs. Gold(19:15) Technologie & Philosophie(21:46) Das Ende der Inflation(24:43) Kriege & Geld(27:24) Warum Bitcoin der effizienteste Markt der Welt ist(31:34) Intrinsischer Wert(35:46) Eigentum neu definiert(39:24) Wie Bitcoin unser Konsumverhalten und den Wohlstand verändert(44:03) Warum am Ende kein Weg an Bitcoin vorbeiführt(47:58) Ausblick in die Zukunft]]>

item.title: VERIFIED by Bitcoin Suisse – Bitcoin's Worst Month Since the ETFs. Is the Bottom In?
item.description:
In this episode, our Head Research Dominic Weibel is joined by crypto protocol expert Wolfgang Vitale and newly-joined senior research associate Filippo Franchini for a dense companion to the bimonthly Industry Roll-Up. 

They unpack June's record $4.5B in US spot ETF outflows alongside a ~20% Bitcoin drawdown, why Strategy's dividend-funded sale of over 3,000 BTC triggered a relief rally rather than a real dump, and Hyperliquid's outlier month of positive flows. From there the conversation turns tactical: a bottom-indicator framework, a potential October cycle low, and a deep dive into Ethereum's roadmap toward what Vitalik Buterin is now calling Ethereum 3.0.

]]>

item.title: The Daily Source Code 863 Bitcoin F.U.B.A.R. Friday – Epic Podcast ~The Daily Source Code 863 Bitcoin F.U.B.A.R. Friday
Bitcoin Rails | Isabel Foxen Duke – Bitcoin's Leading Post-Quantum Signature Proposal | CONDUITION
item.description:
The first fully specified post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin has been proposed to the Bitcoin mailing list.

The proposal introduces a full specification for “SHRINCS,” a hash-based signature scheme initially conceived by Jonas Nick and Mikhail Kudinov of Blockstream Research — with specification details added by new co-authors Conduition, Remix7531 and BIP 360 co-author Ethan Heilman.

Today, I’m honored to share a full whiteboard explanation of the scheme by its co-author Conduition, as well as thorough discussion of the scheme’s key tradeoffs when compared to Bitcoin’s existing elliptic-curve signatures and competing post-quantum alternatives.

In more detail, this interview includes:

— A full whiteboard walkthrough of the scheme’s key components and its relationship to the NIST-standardized scheme SPHINCS+

— SHRINCs’ introduction of a compact stateful path - yes, I said stateful 🌶️

— Whiteboard explanations of all relevant cryptographic subschemes, including FORS, WOTS+C, and XMSS

— Thorough discussion of the scheme’s tradeoffs and implications for Bitcoin’s existing functionality

If you have a vested interest in understanding what may be the future signature scheme protecting Bitcoin transactions in a post-quantum world, this episode is a must-watch.

WARNING: this episode is fairly technical — don't beat yourself up if you don't catch everything, or need to watch it a few times to grok the details.

This episode of Bitcoin Rails is brought to you by:

LayerTwo Labs @LayerTwoLabs — developing research, software, and technologies for scaling Bitcoin via the integration of Drivechains (BIP 300/301)

Hashi on @SuiNetwork — a primitive for executing Bitcoin DeFi transactions, without having to trust a federated bridge or other centralized entity

BitBox @BitBoxSwiss — an open-source Bitcoin-only hardware wallet, with smooth UX and no compromises on security. Check out Bitbox [dot] swiss and use code BITCOINRAILS to get a discount

]]>

item.title: Nerd Culture • A Gamekings Podcast – #274 over Street Fighter, The Batman, filmposters & Trading Card Games
item.description:
Nerd Culture #274 is ook te bekijken op https://youtu.be/zOIKrYQ3jPg 

Ook deze week word je weer bijgepraat over het allerlaatste nerdnieuws in aflevering 274 van Nerd Culture! Dit keer wederom met twee man sterk, want Koos heeft zijn handen vol met poepluiers, en Jelle is na het GTA 6-debacle even ondergedoken. Daarom schuift Daan weer eens aan de desk bij Huey. De evengoed pas geworden vader weet precies hoe je een controller moet vasthouden met een baby op je borst, maar heeft ook net zijn eerste werkweek weer gehad op Gamescom, en daar buit meegenomen in een uniek tasje om bij Nerd Culture mee te komen pronken. Wat zal het zijn? Dat, maar ook het laatste superheldennieuws, en ander nieuws uit de filmwereld hoor en zie je in deze aflevering van Nerd Culture.

Trading Card Games als hobby/verdienmodel & een zoektocht naar kwalitatieve filmposters

Je zuurverdiende centen nog tijdens je werk uitgeven kan blijkbaar het beste op Gamescom. Daan trekt zijn stash open van Magic: The Gathering, One Piece en zelfs een pakje Yu-Gi-Oh kaarten. Hoe diep zit hij inmiddels in deze scene en hoeveel van zijn kaarten heeft 'ie in hoesjes gehezen? Huey heeft ook weer een eigen zoektocht opgezet naar kwalitatieve filmposters. Oud, nieuw, maakt niet veel uit, zolang het maar geen stalen platen zijn en in een lijst kan hangen. Het verdwijnen van de EXPO is voor Huey een groot gemis, dus laten we hem helpen in de comments!

Lucas Museum, Street Fighter vs. Mortal Kombat & de verschillende era's superheldenfilms

De twee staan even stil bij wat trailers, waaronder die van Street Fighter. Wat zijn hun gedachten over de trailer, en hoe verhoudt deze zich tot de Mortal Kombat films? Het lijkt alsof een nieuw tijdperk van videogame-adaptaties aanbreekt dat lekker zondagse B-films gaat produceren. Mocht je toevallig in Los Angeles zijn, kun je altijd even een uitstapje maken naar het Lucas Museum waar Huey deze week graag zijn spreekbeurt over geeft. En tot slot duiken zij in het laatste superheldennieuws, waar een mooie discussie uit voortvloeit over de verschillende tijdperken van superhelden, maar ook over de Fast & Furious filmreeks. Spoiler alert: Huey zit meer op een lijn met zijn meest geliefde director Nolan dan hij denkt. Hoe dat allemaal zit? Dat zie en hoor je in aflevering #274 van Nerd Culture!

Wil je adverteren bij de podcast Nerd Culture óf misschien bij een andere podcast van ILVY Network? Mail dan naar management@ilvy.com en/of kijk even op de website: https://ilvy.com/podcast

See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

]]>

item.title: Bald in Bitcoin – Bald in Bitcoin - Folge 13: Die stille Steuer – Warum der Staat Inflation nicht bekämpfen will
item.description:
Deine Eltern haben dir gesagt: Leg Geld zurück. Sparen lohnt sich.

Guter Rat – damals. Aber heute ist etwas kaputt.

In Folge 12 haben wir gezeigt, warum dein Kontostand stabil aussehen kann und du trotzdem ärmer wirst. Heute gehen wir einen Schritt weiter und stellen die unbequeme Frage dahinter: Warum wird Inflation nicht einfach abgestellt?

Die Antwort: Weil das System genau so gebaut ist.

DAS LERNST DU IN DIESER FOLGE

– Warum Staaten gigantische Schulden durch Inflation heimlich entwerten – Was finanzielle Repression bedeutet – und warum das kein Verschwörungsmythos ist – Wer wirklich die Rechnung zahlt: die stille Steuer auf deine Ersparnisse – Warum das 2%-Ziel der EZB keine zufällige Zahl ist – Was Bitcoin als mengenmäßig begrenztes System damit zu tun hat

WEITERFÜHRENDE EMPFEHLUNGEN

Der Bitcoin-Standard – Saifedean Ammous Schulden: Die ersten 5000 Jahre – David Graeber Reinhart & Sbrancia: The Liquidation of Government Debt (Studie, englisch)

VOR-ORT-KURS – 30. MAI 2026

Bitcoin für Einsteiger – digitales Geld für analog Geborene. Kein Trading. Kein Hype. Einfach ein ruhiger, verständlicher Einstieg. https://bitucation.com/kurs/vor-ort-bitcoin

Hinweis: In dieser Folge wird neben meiner Stimme eine KI-generierte Expertenstimme für technische Erklärpassagen eingesetzt. Alle Inhalte werden von mir recherchiert und geprüft.

⚠️ Keine Finanzberatung. Ausschließlich Bildung und persönliche Perspektive.

]]>

Raoul Pal welcomes back Jordi Visser for a wide-ranging conversation on AI, Bitcoin, tokenization, bonds, productivity, and the future of markets. The guys explore why the panic around bond yields may be overdone, and how AI-driven productivity is already showing up in corporate profits. Then they break down how tokenization could disrupt asset management, why 24/7 markets may favor bots over humans,  and why the next phase of crypto may be about far more than just price. Today's episode is supported by Pyth Network, the fastest-growing name in market data, and probably the only one you can check out for free. Vorige week zagen we een waarschuwingslampje oplichten op het dashboard van de wereldeconomie: op de obligatiemarkt, de plek waar overheden hun geld lenen.En deze week greep Amerika opnieuw in: eerder deze maand in Japan en nu op de eigen obligatiemarkt. Alles in een poging om beleggers gerust te stellen, nu de spanning rondom de ooit zo veilige staatsobligaties oploopt. Terwijl juist die obligatierente doorwerkt in álles: van hypotheken en bedrijfsleningen tot aandelenkoersen, staatsfinanciën en uiteindelijk ook jouw portemonnee.Maar de vraag die boven de markt hangt: werkte deze tweede ingreep eigenlijk wel? En wat kunnen we nu verwachten? De markten zien het al aankomen en daarom schieten goud, zilver en bitcoin omhoog.Hoe dit precies zit, vertel ik je vandaag in deze aflevering.

item.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute – Spotlight Series Ep. 2: Rep. Nick Begich
item.description:
Rep. Nick Begich (R-AK) reached Congress by an unusual route: founding software companies and holding Bitcoin since 2013. BPI's David Zell sat down with him at PubKey to talk about how a builder's instincts shape the way he legislates, his bill to give the U.S. a strategic Bitcoin reserve, and the policy questions AI is raising faster than Washington can answer them.


The conversation runs from Begich's 440 coins on Mt. Gox, to the American Reserve Modernization Act (ARMA), the ~93-year cycle of global reserve currencies, the "untethering" of money from scarcity, and why he believes AI's hardest problem is the "disintermediation of purpose" rather than unemployment. They close on UBI, Alaska's Permanent Fund as a model of citizen ownership, and what's next for the budget and healthcare.


Guest: Rep. Nick Begich (R-AK)

Host: David Zell, Bitcoin Policy Institute

Recorded at PubKey


CHAPTERS

0:00 Intro: A Founder Comes to Congress

1:21 From Baylor to Ford to Building a Software Company

5:17 Finding Bitcoin in 2013 & Surviving Mt. Gox

6:44 The Founder's Mindset vs. the Zero-Sum Worldview

13:56 ARMA: The Case for a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve

19:25 The "Untethering Event": Scarcity, Inflation & the Debt Spiral

25:58 AI's Promise, Peril & the "Disintermediation of Purpose"

31:59 Open-Source AI, China & Catastrophic Misuse Risk

39:14 Drawing the Regulatory Line & the "Bitcoin of AI"

42:25 UBI vs. Alaska's Permanent Fund: "Universal Basic Investment"

49:43 What's Next: The Budget, Healthcare & Quantum


#Bitcoin #BitcoinPolicy #ARMA #NickBegich #AIPolicy #DigitalAssets #StrategicBitcoinReserve #BPI #Crypto #MonetaryPolicy

]]>

item.title: The Bitcoin Treasury Podcast – Smart Money Is On The Wrong Side Of Bitcoin
item.description:
Michael Sullivan joins the show to explain why he published the most bullish piece of his bear market at $63K, and why Bitcoin ripped 15% in 48 hours right after. Michael spent thirteen years as a fintech engineer and writes fiction on the side, and he's turned both into a methodology: measuring the emotion in how Bitcoiners actually talk, cohort by cohort, week by week. His argument is that when every trader is bored, fearful, and rotating into AI and quantum, that isn't a bear signal.

2:34 Why apathy produces the biggest moves

12:26 From fintech engineer and novelist to language analysis

item.title: Ask a Bitcoiner 21 Questions – He Lost $750,000 in Bitcoin. His Hardware Wallet Wasn’t Even the Problem.
item.description:
“The guy who moved his Bitcoin into an exchange in Australia, but his computer had been hacked. He moved the coins from the Coldcard to the exchange. The hackers were just waiting for his funds to move. They used his 2FA and they sold his 70 $750,000 worth of bitcoin.”


Since the Coldcard exploit, there have been a growing number of attacks on people holding Bitcoin. 


In this full interview, Stefan Smith, a Bitcoin specialist with the Bitcoin Adviser, and I discuss how to keep your Bitcoin secure. 


🏆 $50 worth of Bitcoin in this episode (71,000 sats) 🥳


🔎 There’s a hidden 12-word seed phrase in this episode. Find all 12 words + the passphrase and sweep the wallet. 


Here’s how to do it:


  1. Watch the full video and look out for clues. The answer to each clue is a seed word. There are 12 clues in this video.
  2. Follow & Subscribe to Ask a Bitcoiner 21 Questions on socials for passphrase clues.
  3. Once you have all 12 words and the passphrase, sweep the wallet.


Not sure how to recover a wallet? Start here Start here 👉 https://youtu.be/XoaSEvUUCmU

X: https://x.com/noufsmith

Robin Seyr is the host of the Robin Seyr show and one of the hardest-working Bitcoin creators in the space. He is on the brink of reaching 900 episodes on this podcast and will eventually even hit 1,000 episodes later this year.
